chunks: And it is narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:
A man said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “May I be your ransom, when I completed my rites for the ʿUmrah, I went to my wife while I had not trimmed my hair.”
He عليه السلام said: “A camel is upon you.”
He said, “When I intended that from her, while she had not trimmed her hair either, she resisted; then when I overpowered her, she cut off some of her hair with her teeth.”
He عليه السلام said: “May Allah have mercy on her. She was more understanding than you. A camel is upon you, and there is nothing upon her.”

key_terms.أَتَيْتُ أَهْلِي: I went to my wife, meaning I engaged in marital relations
key_terms.أَفْقَهَ: more understanding and knowledgeable of the ruling
key_terms.أُقَصِّرْ: trim my hair as part of exiting the ritual state
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a camel to be offered as expiation
key_terms.عَلَيْهَا شَيْءٌ: any legal liability or expiation upon her
key_terms.نُسُكِي: my ritual acts of devotion performed for ʿUmrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone has marital relations before trimming the hair after ʿUmrah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who has completed the rites of ʿUmrah but engages in intimacy before trimming the hair and exiting the state connected to the ritual. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the man must offer a camel as expiation, while the woman bears no liability in this case, and praises her for recognizing the ruling better than he did.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2751 - It is narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
A man said to Imam Abu Abdullah (as), "May I be your ransom! After completing my rituals for ‘Umrah, I went to my wife but had not trimmed my hair."
Imam (as) said: "You must offer a camel as expiation."
The man then said: "When I attempted this with her, and she had not trimmed her hair either, she resisted. When I overpowered her, she bit off some of her hair with her teeth."
Imam (as) said: "May Allah (swt) have mercy on her. She was more understanding of the matter than you. You must offer a camel as expiation, but nothing is required of her."
